title: How Does a Pufferfish Puff Up? 🐡
description:
How does a pufferfish puff up? It gulps seawater into a folded, stretchy stomach that can expand up to 100 times, so its body balloons to about three times its size with spines sticking out.

Sources:
https://www.texassaltwaterfishingmagazine.com/fishing/education/science-sea/a-swell-adaptation

https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/60545/do-pufferfish-hold-their-breath-while-inflating-themselves

Animated in the Kawaii Anime style.

topic: What happens when a pufferfish puffs up?
script: A pufferfish stomach stretches 100 times bigger, and you'd never guess why it has to. When a hungry fish gets close, the pufferfish opens its mouth wide and gulps seawater, fast. Gulp after gulp, it pumps the water into its stomach. That stomach is folded like an accordion, so it unfolds and keeps on stretching. There are almost no ribs in the way, so the whole body balloons out. Its stretchy skin pulls tight, and little spines pop up all over. Now it's about three times its size, a spiky ball way too big to swallow. But puffing up is hard work. It can take hours to catch its breath, so it only puffs when it has to. Then it spits the water back out. So if you were a pufferfish, what would make you puff?
key_facts: Pufferfish inflate by gulping water into their stomach, not air (in water)
The folded stomach can expand roughly 50-100 times (Texas Saltwater Fishing Magazine)
Puffers lack ribs (or most ribs) and a pelvis, so the body can become a ball
Stretchy collagen-rich skin goes taut; spines stand up
Inflated balloonfish reach about 3x normal volume (3-4x per Mental Floss)
Recovery: heavy breathing for up to about 5 hours afterward (Mental Floss)
